relevance_reason: The abstract reports two patients with severe invasive infections who carried new IRAK2 variants, along with functional data showing reduced TRAF6 ubiquitination and reduced TNF-alpha production. It gives no evidence of autoimmunity or autoinflammation, so it only provides context for IRAK2-related immune dysregulation.

findings.statement: Amali et al. (2024) described 2 patients with sequential or repeated invasive infections. One had hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis triggered by herpes simplex virus, together with tuberculosis. The other had Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia and candidemia.
quotes: In two patients with sequential or repeated invasive infections: herpes simplex virus-triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with tuberculosis, and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia respectively, novel mutations of IRAK2 were identified.

findings.statement: Amali et al. (2024) identified new IRAK2 variants in 2 patients with severe invasive infections. The variants impaired the ability to ubiquitinate the signal adaptor TRAF6 and reduced TNF-alpha production. The authors suggested that IRAK2 may play a central role in host defense against infection.
quotes: novel mutations of IRAK2 were identified

These mutations compromised the capacity to ubiquinate (or functionally modify) the signal adaptor tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 6. The result is impairment of the cytokine tumor necrosis factor-alpha production.
This susceptibility to a varied range of pathogens underlines a potential central role played by IRAK2 in mediating host defense in infectious diseases.
